title: Add contextual anchoring eval gate and progressive rollback CI hook
author: Maya Chen
description: This PR introduces a new evaluation gate — the Contextual Anchoring Consistency (CAC) gate — and a progressive rollback CI hook that triggers automated mitigations when anchor-consistency regressions are detected. Motivation: existing prompt-set regression checks focus on output-level metrics (accuracy, BLEU-like scores, token-level divergence) but do not isolate whether regressions are due to context-dependent brittleness (prompt-length/context-ordering) vs semantic model degradation. CAC computes a per-prompt anchor-consistency score by replaying a small set of "contextual anchors" (minimal context variants, paraphrases, truncated/extended contexts) and measuring stability of structured outputs and key-field extraction. The gate runs as part of the CI eval stage for PRs touching prompt sets, transforms, or scoring logic and will: 1) fail the CI when the weighted anchor-consistency delta exceeds a configurable threshold, 2) attach a prioritized list of failing anchors with deterministic rerun seeds, and 3) optionally trigger the progressive rollback hook which attempts a staged mitigation: re-run on identical compute with expanded sampling, then run the auto-replay augmentation (adds paraphrase/augmentation shots) and finally produce a suggested patch (prompt tweak or anchor whitelist) to reduce false-positives. The PR contains: - a new module eval_harness/gates/contextual_anchor_gate.py implementing CAC metric and gate interface - a lightweight anchor-sampler eval_harness/anchors/sampler.py that generates anchor variants and records canonicalization diffs - a CI hook integration scripts/ci/hooks/progressive_rollback.py that orchestrates reruns and artifacts upload - updates to CI pipeline config .github/workflows/eval-ci.yml to insert the gate into the eval stage - dashboard instrumentation hooks in observability/eval_metrics.ts to emit anchor_consistency.delta and anchor_failures.top_k - unit+integration tests under tests/eval/gates/test_contextual_anchor.py and smoke tests in tests/ci/test_progressive_rollback.py The description below documents design decisions, expected failure modes, and operational runbook for on-call teams. Design notes: CAC is intentionally conservative — it uses median-based aggregation across anchors, confidence normalization for low-token outputs, and a short-circuit to mark prompts as "non-anchorable" if anchors are semantically ambiguous. The progressive rollback hook is opt-in per-repo and scoped to eval-harness; when enabled it will not auto-merge patches but will open a suggested-changes PR with annotations and run a second eval pass on the suggested patch. Operational runbook: - When CI fails due to CAC, the failing anchors will be listed in the CI artifact and triage panel. - Triage: run the provided rerun command (scripts/ci/hooks/progressive_rollback.py --replay-id=<id>) to reproduce locally. - If anchors exhibit acceptable variance (human judgement), add them to anchor-whitelist.yaml in the prompt-set; if not, follow the suggested patch or escalate to ENG-5834. Backwards compatibility: gate is additive and off by default; enabling requires a single flag in repo_eval_config.yaml. This PR also includes docs and a shortguide at docs/eval/contextual_anchors.md.

release_notes: - Introduce Contextual Anchoring Consistency (CAC) gate to detect context-dependent prompt regressions. - Add progressive rollback CI hook to automate reruns and propose mitigations when CAC fails. - Opt-in gate controlled via repo_eval_config.yaml; include runbook and docs at docs/eval/contextual_anchors.md.
operational_impact: Opt-in additive gate; minimal perf overhead in CI because anchor sampling defaults to 5 anchors per prompt and runs on a small subset (smoke cohort). When enabled teams should expect additional eval time (~30-90s per PR depending on prompt-set size) and new CI artifacts. On-call should follow runbook in docs/eval/contextual_anchors.md for triage.
notes_for_qa: QA: run tests/eval/gates/test_contextual_anchor.py locally with --runslow to cover canonicalization heuristics; simulate a failing case by replacing a single model response in tests/fixtures/anchors/ to ensure the gate produces a failure artifact and the progressive rollback hook opens a suggested patch branch.
related_work: Inspired by earlier stability and cohort-based gates (see ENG-4890 prompt stability work). Complements prompt drift detectors by targeting context-sensitive variance (length/order/paraphrase).
